export function berthsFor(boat: Boat, berths: Berth[], needPower: boolean): BerthId[] {
  return berths
    .map((berth, index) => ({ berth, index }))
    .filter(({ berth }) => berth.boatId === "" && fits(boat, berth) && (!needPower || berth.power))
    .sort((a, b) => a.berth.length - b.berth.length || a.index - b.index)
    .map(({ berth }) => berth.id);
}

I added `berthsFor` at the end of `src/moorings.ts`. It filters to free berths that `fits` accepts (and have power when `needPower` is true), then sorts by length with the original index as a tie-breaker. It works on a new array, so `berths` and its berths are not changed.

I couldn't see the file, so these are guesses to check:
- `fits` takes `(boat, berth)` and returns a boolean.
- A berth has the fields `id`, `length`, `power` (truthy when powered) and `boatId`.
- `Boat`, `Berth` and `BerthId` are already in scope in that file.

If any name differs, adjust that line.
